analysis.summary: Norway enter Matchday 2 as Group I leaders after a commanding 4-1 demolition of Iraq, with Erling Haaland scoring twice on his World Cup debut. Senegal must avoid defeat to maintain any realistic path to the knockout rounds after a 3-1 opening loss to France, in which they were competitive for 45 minutes but capitulated in the second half. This is a high-stakes encounter for Senegal, who carry dangerous attacking weapons in Mane, Jackson and Sarr but face a Norway side brimming with confidence around an in-form Haaland. The neutral MetLife Stadium venue marginally reduces Norway's notional home advantage.
analysis.home_form: Norway won 4-1 v Iraq (World Cup MD1, June 16) with Haaland scoring at 29' and 44', Ostigard heading a corner goal at 76', plus an own goal. In pre-tournament friendlies: W 3-1 v Sweden (June 1), D 1-1 v Morocco (June 7). World Cup qualifying: unbeaten, 8W 0D 0L, 37 goals scored in 8 matches including an 11-0 v Moldova and a 4-1 win at San Siro v Italy.
analysis.away_form: Senegal lost 3-1 to France (World Cup MD1, June 16) - competitive first half but conceded three in the second 45; Mbappe brace and Barcola goal, Mbaye pulled one back late. Pre-tournament friendlies showed strong form: W 3-1 v England (Wembley, June 2025), W 2-0 v Brazil (away). World Cup qualifying: unbeaten, 7W 3D 0L from 10 games in CAF Group B. Won AFCON 2025 title (subsequently stripped by CAF over protest incident in the final).
analysis.h2h: Only one prior senior meeting: Senegal 1-0 Norway (friendly, March 2006). No meaningful competitive head-to-head history exists between these sides.
injuries_news: Norway: No confirmed injuries reported. David Moller Wolfe and Julian Ryerson had minor concerns post-Iraq but are expected available. Side expected to be largely unchanged from MD1.

Senegal: No confirmed injuries or suspensions reported ahead of MD2. Full squad appears available. Pape Thiaw (head coach) faced a CAF suspension threat but is expected to be on the touchline. Ibrahim Mbaye may contest for a starting berth after scoring as a substitute vs France.
Sadio Mane: Named in Senegal's 26-man World Cup squad and started against France; fit and available.
key_factors: Haaland vs Senegal's central defence: Haaland scored twice against Iraq and his aerial and physical presence will test Koulibaly and the Senegal backline throughout.
Senegal's must-win pressure: With 0 points from MD1, Senegal essentially need a win or draw here to remain alive; this compels them to attack, potentially opening space for Norway on the counter.
Ødegaard as creator: Martin Ødegaard was central to Norway's attacking play against Iraq and his link-up play with Haaland is a primary threat.
Senegal's attack potent but second-half fragility: The trio of Mane, Sarr and Jackson has quality to threaten any defense, but France exposed Senegal's tendency to fade in the second half.
Neutral venue at altitude/heat: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, NJ) is a sea-level outdoor venue with humid June conditions - no significant altitude advantage for either side.
Group standing stakes: Norway win secures early qualification; Senegal must avoid elimination. France vs Iraq plays simultaneously, making goal difference relevant.
